newsitem.title: SPAIN: Iberdrola buys controlling stake in Brazil's Coelba.
newsitem.headline: Iberdrola buys controlling stake in Brazil's Coelba.

text.p: A consortium led by Iberdrola Thursday bought a controlling stake in Brazilian power distributor Coelba for $1.6 billion, boosting the Spanish utility's plans to compete in Latin America.

"This is a big company and wonderful news," said Ramon Forcada, utilities analyst at Ibersecurities in Madrid. "Internationalization has been one of Iberdrola's pending assignments...This is a very important step forward."

The consortium, which also includes Brazil's largest pension fund Previ and Banco do Brazil's brokerage arm BB DTVM, beat out four other offers for the 65.64 percent stake of Coelba voting capital, bidding 77.3 percent above the minimum price.

Iberdrola, Spain's second-largest utility, has been making headway in Latin America, and earlier this month another consortium in which it took part won a controlling stake in Rio de Janeiro state gas company CEG and piped gas distributor Riogas.
Coelba is owned by the impoverished northern Brazilian state of Bahia, where it operates.
